title: Mining Statistics Cheat Sheet
question: What are the statistical methods mining companies actually use, from assay QA/QC and geostatistics to sampling theory, reliability and project economics, each applied and interpreted on data?
one_liner: Runnable, annotated analysis scripts, each printing an interpretation of what it computed, condensed into a one-page method chooser.
aim: Document the statistical methods used in mining, as runnable, annotated examples with assumptions, interpretation and failure modes stated for each.
scope: Assay exploratory analysis and capping, compositional data, QA/QC, geostatistics, sampling theory, equipment reliability, safety rates, project economics and environmental compliance trends.
conclusion: Runnable reference with generated worked-example results; no new scientific study is claimed.
finding: Each script applies one family of methods to real or clearly labelled synthetic data and prints an interpretation, so the output reads like a worked example. The cheat sheet is the index: a table from question to method to script section, with the assumptions and the failure modes beside each.

traps.how: Values below detection are handled by Kaplan-Meier and ROS, never substitution, in the QA/QC and environmental sections.
Compositional data: percentages and ppm are closed, so log-ratio transforms precede biplots and models.
Lab bias and precision are measured with CRM control charts, CUSUM and duplicate analysis before assays are trusted.
Declustering corrects the preferential-sampling bias of drilling where the grade is high.

figures.caption: Estimates compared with exhaustive block truth; the uncertainty panel shows mean point variance, not block-estimate uncertainty.
Seeded synthetic certified-reference-material controls and planted laboratory bias.

not_claimed: A reference, not a study; no new empirical finding is claimed.
data: Public and synthetic assay, duplicate, variogram, reliability, safety, price and water-quality datasets
